root_cause.text: In XFS `xlog_alloc_log()`, the log cache roundoff (`l_iclog_roundoff`) incorrectly fell back to `BBSIZE`/512 bytes when `sb_logsunit` was unset, even though the on-disk log sector size (`sb_logsectsize`) could be 4096, producing an undersized roundoff that corrupted log writes and broke mount/recovery.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `else if (mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize > 0) log->l_iclog_roundoff = mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize; else log->l_iclog_roundoff = BBSIZE;`, and the CVE text explains that when the superblock has `sectsz=4096` and `sunit=0`, “the roundoff factor is 512, not 4096 as you'd expect,” which “leads to corrupt logs and unmountable filesystems.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: XFS’s log allocation code (`xlog_alloc_log()` in `fs/xfs/xfs_log.c`) fell back to a fixed `BBSIZE`/512-byte `l_iclog_roundoff` when no log stripe unit was set, instead of using the log sector size (`sb_logsectsize`), allowing misaligned 4K-sector logs to be built and later corrupted during mount/recovery.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `xlog_alloc_log()` from `else log->l_iclog_roundoff = BBSIZE;` to `else if (mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize > 0) log->l_iclog_roundoff = mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize;`, and the CVE description explicitly says that when `log sectsz=4096 sunit=0`, “the roundoff factor is 512, not 4096 as you'd expect,” which “leads to corrupt logs and unmountable filesystems.”

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence supports the specific fix, but the proposed root cause is too imprecise and slightly inconsistent with the patch/CVE. The bug is not simply that it “fell back to a fixed BBSIZE/512-byte roundoff instead of using the log sector size” in general; the issue is that when `sb_logsunit` is absent, `xlog_alloc_log()` used `BBSIZE` even though `sb_logsectsize` could be 4096, causing an undersized `l_iclog_roundoff`. Also, the evidence claims a 4K-sector log is “built and later corrupted during mount/recovery,” but the CVE/commit emphasize that the bad roundoff value itself leads to corrupt logs and mount/recovery failure on malformed or broken mkfs filesystems. The root cause should more directly explain that the code chose the wrong fallback size for log roundoff when no log stripe unit was configured, resulting in a roundoff smaller than the on-disk log sector size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the superblock log sector size for iclog roundoff when available, falling back to BBSIZE otherwise.
intent_record.what: In xlog_alloc_log(), an additional conditional branch was added so that log->l_iclog_roundoff is set to mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize when sb_logsunit is not used and sb_logsectsize is greater than 0; otherwise it still falls back to BBSIZE.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the log buffer roundoff now respects the filesystem's log sector size when available, instead of always defaulting to the base block size. This changes the alignment/rounding used for iclog allocation and can avoid using an incorrect default size on systems that report a valid log sector size.

candidates.rationale: This fallback hardcodes the iclog roundoff to BBSIZE when sb_logsunit is unset, which is the vulnerable behavior described: it ignores the on-disk log sector size (sb_logsectsize), allowing an undersized roundoff on 4K-log systems and causing corrupted log writes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement hardcodes iclog roundoff to BBSIZE when sb_logsunit is unset, instead of using the on-disk log sector size. On systems with a 4K log sector size, this produces an undersized roundoff and leads to corrupted log writes and mount/recovery failures.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a6a65fef5ef8d0a6a0ce514eb66b2f3dfa777b48
Author: Dave Chinner <dchinner@redhat.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 18 08:21:48 2021 -0700

    xfs: log stripe roundoff is a property of the log
    
    We don't need to look at the xfs_mount and superblock every time we
    need to do an iclog roundoff calculation. The property is fixed for
    the life of the log, so store the roundoff in the log at mount time
    and use that everywhere.
    
    On a debug build:
    
    $ size fs/xfs/xfs_log.o.*
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the old fallback to a byte/block-size roundoff when `sb_logsunit` was unset, which could under-size the log roundoff relative to `sb_logsectsize` (e.g. 4096). In this snippet, that old logic is already replaced by a log-local roundoff property set at mount time: `if (xfs_sb_version_haslogv2(&mp->m_sb) && mp->m_sb.sb_logsunit > 1) log->l_iclog_roundoff = mp->m_sb.sb_logsunit; else log->l_iclog_roundoff = BBSIZE;`. The calculation paths now consistently use `log->l_iclog_roundoff` instead of recalculating from the superblock, e.g. `count = roundup(count_init, log->l_iclog_roundoff);`, `ASSERT(*roundoff < log->l_iclog_roundoff);`, `log->l_curr_block = roundup(log->l_curr_block, BTOBB(log->l_iclog_roundoff));`, and `unit_bytes += 2 * log->l_iclog_roundoff;`. Because the shown code already stores and reuses the roundoff, the previously vulnerable construct is not present here and the fix is already in place.
